texts: After each spring tide, a Cauldron Hall apprentice refills the cisterns from the deep ebb.
The apprentice walks the harbor pier to the deep-ebb point.
A first-year apprentice usually fills the cisterns.

fields.sentence: After each spring tide, a Cauldron Hall apprentice refills the cisterns from the deep ebb.
parse: (: refill_rule (Implication (Member $x spring_tide) (And (Member (sk_refill $x) refill) (Agent (sk_refill $x) (sk_apprentice $x)) (Member (sk_apprentice $x) apprentice) (Possession (sk_apprentice $x) cauldron_hall) (Patient (sk_refill $x) sk_cistern_1) (Source (sk_refill $x) (sk_ebb $x)) (Member (sk_ebb $x) ebb) (Member (sk_ebb $x) deep) (Before $x (sk_refill $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The rule consumes the explicit quantifier word 'each' (it is what sets strength 1.0) but emits no (QuantifierPhrase spring_tide refill "each") companion, which the instruction set calls mandatory for every explicit quantifier word a rule consumes and exempts only for the 'every time / whenever' frequency conditional.

q2_gaps: A universally-quantified temporal-adjunct NP ('after each spring tide'): the instruction set covers 'every time / whenever + CLAUSE' (an occurrence domain, rule form, no QuantifierPhrase companion) and 'every / each + kind SUBJECT' (rule form, companion mandatory), but not a determiner-quantified event-noun inside a temporal PP, so neither the rule routing nor the companion requirement is settled for it.
review.notes: The rest is on doctrine: 'a Cauldron Hall apprentice' takes the proper-noun-premodifier Possession route with the head noun parsed normally, the definite plural 'the cisterns' takes a top-level group witness shared across occurrences, and the per-tide apprentice/ebb are dependent existentials as Skolem functions.

issues.reason: The rule quantifies the named kind range `spring_tide` and consumes the explicit word "each" to set strength 1.0, and the companion is stated mandatory for every explicit quantifier word the rule consumes (*Negation (copular)*), restating exactly a range the rule itself quantifies; the sole carve-out names "every time / whenever", a clause-ranged frequency conditional with no kind symbol to fill the companion's first slot, which is not this case.

gaps_confirmed: Routing for a determiner-quantified event-noun inside a temporal PP ("after each spring tide") is unspecified: the occurrence-rule route is given only for "every time / whenever" CLAUSES and the flat habitual form only for calendar slots (Weekday / Month / Hour terms).
new_gaps: A definite plural object inside such an improvised occurrence rule ("refills the cisterns") has no stated treatment: *Quantifiers, generics & scope* would require a per-member distribution rule for a distributive predicate on a grouped plural, but nesting that rule inside the outer rule's consequent has no licensed shape.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form keeps this rule unchanged and adds the companion `(: tide_q (QuantifierPhrase spring_tide refill "each") (STV 1.0 0.99))` beside it.
adjudication.notes: Everything else is doctrine-clean: the `Possession` route for the proper-noun premodifier "a Cauldron Hall apprentice", the whole-name symbol plus a separate `hall` type atom, the `spring_tide` genus with the noun modifier correctly unexposed, and "after" rendered as `(Before <tide> <refill>)`.

fields.sentence: The apprentice walks the harbor pier to the deep-ebb point.

q1_issues.issue: (Inheritance deep_ebb ebb) decomposes the nested modifier a second level, which 'Decompose once, to single-word lemmas, then stop' does not license — the compound's only licensed decomposition is the head genus at statement 8.

(Inheritance deep_ebb deep) exposes a modifier genus for a sub-compound the parse never introduces as a class of any referent, and 'deep-ebb' fails the predication test on the point, so the modifier should have been left inside the symbol.

q2_gaps: A compound kind whose modifier is itself a multi-word hyphenated unit ('deep-ebb point'): the modifier-exposure test ('can the modifier be predicated of the thing?') and the 'unpack it into single-word parts' wording are both written for a single-word modifier, and the section gives no ruling on whether such a modifier is itself unpacked.
review.notes: The rest is sound: Theme for the traversed pier, Goal for 'to the …point', the head genus (Inheritance deep_ebb_point point), and no tense atom on the bare simple present. Reading 'harbor pier' as whole+part (PartOf) rather than a fused subtype is a judgment the compound rule leaves open, and is defensible.

issues.reason: The cited bar reads 'don't recurse on parts already single' — it stops recursion on single-word parts, while 'unpack it into single-word parts' pulls the other way for a multi-word modifier, so this is exactly the gap the reviewer's own q2 concedes, and (Inheritance deep_ebb ebb) is a true, well-typed definitional genus traceable to the words 'deep-ebb' — acceptable improvisation under the calibration line.

The predication test is applied to the wrong bearer: the parse never emitted (Inheritance deep_ebb_point deep_ebb), and applied to the sub-compound the test passes ('the ebb is deep'), where Compound concepts makes a gradable-adjective modifier genus mandatory ('determined, not optional'), not an over-assertion.

gaps_confirmed: Compound concepts gives no ruling on whether a multi-word modifier inside a fused compound ('deep-ebb' in 'deep-ebb point') is itself decomposed — 'decompose once, then stop' and 'unpack it into single-word parts' point in opposite directions, and the modifier-exposure predication test is written for a single-word modifier.
new_gaps: A noun-noun compound naming a built structure inside a geographic facility ('harbor pier') falls between the 'car engine' possessor/whole PartOf route and the 'a place inside a place is LocatedIn, never PartOf' bar; no test says which head applies when the whole is a place and the part is a structure.
adjudication.notes: The rest conforms: Theme for the traversed pier, Goal for 'to the … point', the head genus (Inheritance deep_ebb_point point), definite referents typed, and no status atom on the bare simple present.

fields.sentence: A first-year apprentice usually fills the cisterns.
parse: (: fill_bundle (And (Member sk_fill_1 fill) (Agent sk_fill_1 sk_apprentice_1) (Member sk_apprentice_1 first_year_apprentice) (Patient sk_fill_1 sk_cistern_1)) (STV 0.8 0.99))

q1_issues.issue: A positive event is asserted as one (And ...) bundle at strength 0.8, but the instruction set reserves the single-conjunction form for the strength-0 denial (a positive event is separate atoms); bundling also drags the subject's typing atom down to 0.8.

'usually' is an explicit frequency-quantifier word the claim consumes, so the mandatory QuantifierPhrase companion recording that word is missing — without it a hedged habitual is indistinguishable from an unhedged claim that merely carries a lowered strength.

q2_gaps: a frequency adverb ('usually') over a habitual clause whose subject is an indefinite singular — doctrine makes 'a first-year apprentice' a witness rather than a generic, but the frequency dial's two channels only set a distributing rule's strength or a flat generic statement's strength, so a multi-atom witness-subject event has no licensed carrier for the adverb
review.notes: Correct calls: indefinite singular subject taken as a witness rather than a kind generic, definite plural 'the cisterns' as a GroupOf group witness, first_year_apprentice fused with genus apprentice and no modifier genus, and no status atom on the present habitual.

issues.reason: Negation (events) states the shape flatly — "Positive event = separate atoms; negated event = one strength-0.0 conjunction" — and folding the subject's typing atom (Member sk_apprentice_1 first_year_apprentice) into a 0.8 bundle hedges a fact the sentence states unhedged (only the frequency of filling is hedged, not that the person is a first-year apprentice).

The half that stands: the surface word "usually" is left with no record at all, and the companion is called "mandatory for every explicit quantifier word the rule or claim consumes (including a frequency adverb's word)"; the half that does not stand: the same rule bars a companion restating "a range that appears nowhere else in the parse", and this witness-subject parse quantifies no first_year_apprentice range for (QuantifierPhrase first_year_apprentice fill "usually") to restate.

gaps_confirmed: a frequency adverb over a habitual whose subject doctrine forces to a witness (indefinite singular + verbal predicate) has no carrier: the dial's two channels set a distributing rule's strength or a flat generic statement's strength, and a multi-atom witness-subject event is neither
new_gaps: QuantifierPhrase's slots are (kind, verb-lemma), so a frequency adverb consumed by a witness-subject event has no well-formed companion instance at all — the surface word is unrecordable here, not merely unrecorded
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form emits the fill event as separate atoms with the subject's typing and the role atoms at (STV 1.0 0.99) and no bundle; since the instruction set licenses no carrier for "usually" over a witness-subject event, its own fallback applies — carry the qualifier or leave the whole claim out and record the gap, never re-scope the hedge onto atoms the sentence does not hedge.
adjudication.notes: Correct on everything else: indefinite singular subject as a witness rather than a kind generic, definite plural "the cisterns" as a group witness, first_year_apprentice fused with genus apprentice and the noun modifier unexposed, and no status atom on the habitual present.
